topic: Emotion regulation across mental health conditions
text:
A 2026 meta-analysis pooled 188 studies comparing adults living with one of 15 mental health conditions and adults without a diagnosis. Across all 12 conditions analysed with the most widely used questionnaire, people living with a condition reported more difficulty regulating their emotions. Two everyday strategies told a similar story. In almost every condition studied, people living with a condition reported rethinking situations less often and holding back the outward expression of feelings more often.

Why this matters across roles: The authors describe emotion regulation difficulty as a transdiagnostic feature, so how a person manages strong feelings may be a shared thread worth noticing, whatever the diagnosis and whatever your role.

One practical takeaway: Within your role, it may be worth asking with curiosity how a person usually handles strong feelings, for example whether they tend to rethink what happened or keep feelings to themselves, and with the person's consent, sharing what you learn with their treating team where appropriate.

Where the evidence stops:
• Every study relied on self-report questionnaires.
• Most studies were cross-sectional, so we cannot tell whether these patterns come before or after a condition develops.
• Only adult samples were included.

Key source: Sloan et al., 2026: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41398-026-04119-x
